designSummary: Case-control study with frequency matching by discharge quarter and ward group; exposure is an attended meeting with a written plan.
sampleSize: With 160 cases and 320 controls and an exposure prevalence of about 25 percent among controls, the study has about 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect an odds ratio of 0.50, and about 67 percent power for 0.55; smaller effects would be estimated imprecisely. 480 notes at fifteen minutes each use the 120 approved hours. The estimate will be reported with its confidence interval rather than as a significance verdict.
primaryAnalysis: Unconditional logistic regression of case status on the exposure, adjusted for the two matching factors and six complexity measures fixed in advance (prior admissions in 12 months, frailty score, living alone, dementia, number of regular medicines, discharge destination); about 16 cases per parameter.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model with the three-level exposure (attended with plan, booked but not attended, none); 7-day readmission among cases; an exploratory interaction with living alone reported without a significance claim.
missingData: Notes in which attendance cannot be determined are counted and reported; the primary analysis treats them as a separate category, with sensitivity analyses coding them first as exposed and then as unexposed; complexity measures missing for more than 5 percent are handled by multiple imputation.
multiplicity: One primary contrast; secondary and exploratory estimates are reported with confidence intervals and labelled as such.
software: R; the abstraction form, covariate list and analysis code archived before reading starts.
summary: 160 cases and 320 controls give about 80 percent power for an odds ratio of 0.50; adjusted logistic regression with complexity covariates fixed in advance.
